In what year was Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex born?
Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex (Henry Charles Albert David; born 15 September 1984), is a member of the British royal family.

Yitzhak Rabin: Rabin was born in Jerusalem to Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe and was raised in a Labor Zionist household.

Julius Caesar: A member of the First Triumvirate, he led the Roman armies through the Gallic Wars and defeated his political rival Pompey in Caesar's civil war.

Jeffrey Dahmer: Dahmer committed his first murder in Ohio in 1978; he did not resume killing until 1987.

Burning Man is a week-long large-scale desert event focused on "community, art, self-expression, and self-reliance" held annually in the Western United States.
In what year was Maya civilization founded?
Maya civilization: The Maya civilization was a Mesoamerican civilization that existed from antiquity to the early modern period.

Labour Party (UK): The Labour Party, commonly Labour, is a political party in the United Kingdom.

Otzma Yehudit: Michael Ben-Ari. It is the ideological descendant of the outlawed Kach party.
Adhan: God in Islam. The five prayer times are known in Arabic as fajr (فجر), dhuhr (ظهر), asr (عصر), maghrib (مغرب), and isha (عشاء).
In which country is Great Molasses Flood?
Great Molasses Flood: United States. The event entered local folklore and residents reported for decades afterwards that the area still smelled of molasses on hot summer days.
In which country was the Kingdom of Cochin?
Kingdom of Cochin: British Raj. It originated in the early part of the 12th century and continued to rule until its accession to the Dominion of India in 1949.
In which country did the Battle of Kunersdorf take place?
Battle of Kunersdorf: Prussia. The Battle of Kunersdorf occurred on 12 August 1759 near Kunersdorf (now Kunowice, Poland) immediately east of Frankfurt an der Oder.
In which country is Avignon Papacy?
Avignon Papacy: France. Clement refused to move to Rome, and in 1309 he moved his court to the papal enclave at Avignon, where it remained for the next 67 years.
In which country is Tsavo Man-Eaters?
Tsavo Man-Eaters: East Africa Protectorate. The lion pair was said to have killed dozens of people, with some early estimates reaching over a hundred deaths.

Iranian Embassy siege: United Kingdom. The British government quickly decided that safe passage would not be granted and a siege ensued.
In which country is COYOTE based?
COYOTE: United States. COYOTE is an American sex workers' rights organization.
In which country is Haitian Revolution?
Haitian Revolution: Saint-Domingue. The rebels' organizational capacity and tenacity under pressure inspired stories that shocked and frightened slave owners in the hemisphere.
In which country is Dunkirk evacuation?
Dunkirk evacuation: France. The British Expeditionary Force (BEF) was sent to help defend France.
Which of these is an official language of Safavid dynasty?
Safavid dynasty: Persian. The Safavid dynasty had its origin in the Safavid Sufi order, which was established in the city of Ardabil in the Iranian Azerbaijan region.
Which of these was an official language of Netherlands Antilles?
Which of these was an official language of Zaire?
Zaire: French. It was, by area, the third-largest country in Africa after Sudan and Algeria, and the 11th-largest country in the world from 1965 to 1991.
Which country used the Spanish maravedí as its official currency?
The Spanish maravedí is the official currency of Kingdom of Castile. The Kingdom of Castile was a polity in the Iberian Peninsula during the Middle Ages.
The son of veteran Uttar Pradesh politician Mulayam Singh, this Samajwadi Party president served as the state's youngest-ever Chief Minister from 2012 to 2017 — who is he?
Akhilesh Yadav (born 1 July 1973) is an Indian politician and national president of the Samajwadi Party, who served as the 20th Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh from 2012 to 2017.

This 8th-century Chinese civil war began as a commandery revolt seeking to topple the Tang dynasty, briefly capturing the capital Chang'an before its own leaders turned on each other through a string of assassinations — which uprising?
An Lushan rebellion was a civil war in China that lasted from 755 to 763, at the approximate midpoint of the Tang dynasty (618-907).
A Franco-German joint venture dedicated to culture, this public channel carries two audio tracks so it can serve viewers in both countries at once — what's it called?
Arte (Association relative la tlvision europenne, "Association relating to European television") is a European public service channel dedicated to culture.

In 1757, the British East India Company under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal, an outcome enabled by betrayal and earlier troop commitments to Afghan invaders. What was this decisive battle?
Battle of Plassey was a decisive victory of the British East India Company, under the leadership of Robert Clive, over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies on 23 June 1757.
According to the Book of Genesis, Abraham was commanded to perform this covenant rite on a baby boy's eighth day of life, traditionally carried out by a mohel — what is it called?
Brit milah ("covenant of circumcision"), or bris, is the ceremony of circumcision in Judaism and Samaritanism during which a newborn male's foreskin is surgically removed.
Said to hail from Lycia in Asia Minor, this fire-breathing Greek monster is typically depicted as a lion with a goat's head sprouting from its back and a snake for a tail — what is it?
Chimera (mythology) (ky-MEER-ə, kih-, -MAIR-ə; lit. 'she-goat') was a monstrous fire-breathing hybrid creature in Greek mythology.
Commissioned by a judge's Transylvania Company in 1775, this frontiersman blazed the Wilderness Road through the Cumberland Gap and founded Boonesborough — which early American folk hero?
Daniel Boone was American pioneer and frontiersman (1734–1820).
Raised in Hastinapura to become crown prince, this scheming cousin of the Pandavas relied on allies like Shakuni and Karna to plot against them — who is he?
Duryodhana is the primary antagonist of the Hindu epic Mahabharata.

The stepson of Napoleon Bonaparte through his mother Joséphine's second marriage, this French statesman and military officer served in the Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars and was later adopted by the emperor — who was he?
Eugène de Beauharnais (3 September 1781 - 21 February 1824) was a French statesman and military officer who served in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
Representing Hiroshima's 1st district since 1996, this politician was foreign minister before becoming Japan's prime minister and LDP president in 2021 — who is he?
Fumio Kishida (born 29 July 1957) is a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan and President of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) from 2021 until his resignation in 2024.
Born when a papal bull elevated Cosimo I de' Medici in 1569, this Central Italian monarchy replaced a republic and was ruled by the Medici until their senior branch died out in 1737. What was it?
Grand Duchy of Tuscany was an Italian monarchy located in Central Italy that existed, with interruptions, from 1569 to 1860, replacing the Republic of Florence.

This period of Japanese history corresponds to the reign of Emperor Akihito, beginning the day after the death of his father—posthumously renamed Emperor Shōwa—in January 1989, and ending with Akihito's 2019 abdication. What is this period called?
Heisei era was the period of Japanese history corresponding to the reign of Emperor Akihito from 8 January 1989 until his abdication on 30 April 2019.
Though scholars generally consider her fictional, which legendary Chinese folk heroine is said to have lived during the Northern and Southern dynasties era?
Hua Mulan (traditional; simplified; pinyin: Hu Mln) is a legendary Chinese folk heroine from the Northern and Southern dynasties era (4th to 6th century AD) of Chinese history.
A Manhattan-raised businesswoman and Georgetown-then-Penn graduate, she became a presidential advisor from 2017 to 2021 in her father's White House — who is she?
Ivanka Trump (iv-; born October 30, 1981) is an American businesswoman.
According to the New Testament, this figure is held to be the Son of God whose crucifixion and resurrection are believed to offer humanity salvation and eternal life — who is he?
Jesus in Christianity is the Son of God as chronicled in the Bible's New Testament, and is held to be God the Son, a prosopon (person) of the Trinity of God.
A nephew of Constantine the Great, this Roman emperor rejected Christianity in favor of Neoplatonic paganism, earning him the enduring nickname 'the Apostate' — who was he?
Julian (emperor) (Ancient; 331 - 26 June 363) was the Caesar of the West from 355 to 360 and Roman emperor from 361 to 363, as well as a notable philosopher and author in Greek.
Existing from the mid-12th century to the early 20th, this western Iberian monarchy briefly anchored a transatlantic union with Brazil and the Algarves from 1815 to 1822 — which kingdom?
Kingdom of Portugal was a monarchy in the western Iberian Peninsula and the predecessor of the modern Portuguese Republic.

This Qin dynasty general served under the future First Emperor of China during the conquest of the six rival Warring States kingdoms, and was the great-great-grandfather of a famous Han dynasty general — who is he?
Li Xin (Qin) was an important Chinese military general of Qin during the Warring States era.
This Panamanian military officer ruled his country through puppet presidents in the 1980s, amassing a fortune from drug trafficking despite long ties to American intelligence — who was he?
Manuel Noriega (mahn-WEL; February 11, 1934 - May 29, 2017) was a Panamanian military officer and politician who was the de facto ruler of Panama from 1983 to 1989.

A former physician, this Azerbaijani politician serves as both First Lady and First Vice President of her country — a position her husband, the president, created in 2017 specifically to appoint her to it. Who is she?
Mehriban Aliyeva (ne Pashayeva; born 26 August 1964) is an Azerbaijani politician and former physician who is the First Vice President and First Lady of Azerbaijan.

He earned a law degree from King Saud University and advised his father before being named defence minister in 2015, then crown prince in 2017 — which grandson of Ibn Saud is now the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia?
Mohammed bin Salman (born 31 August 1985), also known as MbS, is the de facto ruler of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, formally serving as Crown Prince and Prime Minister.
Founded in 2020 by a cosmetics-company magnate, this liberal-leaning party takes a moderately supportive stance toward Vladimir Putin while opposing much of the ruling party's agenda — which party?
New People (Russia) is a political party in Russia formed in 2020.

Fought across a 630-kilometre front, this decisive offensive by the Croatian Army recaptured territory held by the self-declared Republic of Serbian Krajina in the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence — which offensive?
Operation Storm (Serbo-) was the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence and a major factor in the outcome of the Bosnian War.
An aristocrat's son and Saint-Cyr graduate, this Free-French World War II general is known in France simply by one name, and was made a Marshal of France posthumously in 1952 — who is he?
Philippe Leclerc de Hauteclocque (22 November 1902 - 28 November 1947) was a Free-French general during World War II.
This consumer-advocate lawyer wrote the 1965 book 'Unsafe at Any Speed,' which helped spur the National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act — who is he?
Ralph Nader (born February 27, 1934) is an American lawyer and political activist involved in consumer protection, environmentalism, and government reform causes.

Born into the Romney family, this Republican strategist chaired the Michigan GOP before leading the Republican National Committee from 2017 until her 2024 resignation, a tenure marked by significant electoral losses — who is she?
Ronna McDaniel (ne Romney; born March 20, 1973) is an American political strategist who served as chair of the Republican National Committee (RNC) from 2017 until her resignation in 2024.
What term, coined by 19th-century Egyptologists, describes a mysterious seafaring confederation blamed for attacks on Egypt and the Eastern Mediterranean around 1200 BC?

Sea Peoples is a phrase used to describe an unidentified seafaring confederation or group of tribes hypothesized to have attacked Egypt and other Eastern Mediterranean regions around 1200 BC during the Late Bronze Age.
In Greek myth, this creature with a woman's head, a lion's body, and a bird's wings killed and ate travelers who failed to solve her riddle. What creature is it?

Founded in the early 1900s by English occultist Aleister Crowley, this esoteric spiritual philosophy centers on discovering and following one's 'True Will,' outlined in a text he said was dictated by a non-corporeal entity — name the movement?
Thelema is a Western esoteric and occult social and spiritual philosophy, and a new religious movement.
This militant leader spent more than 25 years directing an armed campaign against the Sri Lankan government in pursuit of Tamil independence — who is he?

Velupillai Prabhakaran (26 November 1954 - 18 May 2009) was an Eelam Tamil revolutionary, guerrilla leader and a major figure of Tamil nationalism, being the founder and leader of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Aboard Apollo 8 with Borman and Lovell, this astronaut circled the Moon ten times and snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph in December 1968 — who was he?
William Anders (17 October 1933 - 7 June 2024) was a United States Air Force major general, electrical engineer, nuclear engineer, NASA astronaut, and businessman.
Born Ma He into a Muslim family and later castrated into eunuch service, this early Ming dynasty admiral's Indian Ocean voyages vastly expanded China's political and commercial reach — who was he?
Zheng He (Wade-; 1371-1433/1435) was a Chinese admiral and diplomat from the early Ming dynasty.

Nicknamed the 'Sheikh of slaughtering,' this Jordanian militant formed a group in 1999 before pledging allegiance to al-Qaeda's leader in 2004 and masterminding bombings during the Iraq War — who was he?
An Iranic nomadic people connected to the Yancai and Aorsi of ancient sources, this group dominated the Pontic-Caspian steppe before the Goths broke their hold in the 3rd century CE — who were they?
Alans: Ancient Iranic people of the North Caucasus.
Formed in 1993 by merging a party from West Germany with one from East Germany, this party held 85 of the Bundestag's 630 seats after Germany's 2025 election — which party?
Alliance 90/The Greens: Green political party in Germany.
Fought in 1879 between the British Empire and an African kingdom, this conflict included the defeat at Isandlwana and the defence of Rorke's Drift — which conflict?
Anglo-Zulu War: British colonial war in 1879. Two famous battles of the war were the Zulu victory at Isandlwana and the British defence at Rorke's Drift.
After conquering Kalinga in a brutal war around 260 BCE, this third Mauryan emperor turned to Buddhism and helped carry it across ancient Asia — who was he?
Ashoka: Mauryan emperor from 269 to 232 BCE.
This Indian engineer-turned-politician served as Karnataka's 17th chief minister from 2021 to 2023 before becoming a Lok Sabha MP for Haveri — who is he?
Basavaraj Bommai: 23rd Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2021 to 2023. In July 2022, Bommai became only the second person from BJP to complete one year as chief minister of the state.

Serving as Italy's 45th prime minister from 1983 to 1987, this Socialist Party leader ran the fourth-longest government in the Italian Republic before later being convicted of political corruption — who is he?
It began in 1703 as a townhouse for a duke, then George III bought it in 1761 as a private home for Queen Charlotte — today it's a monarch's official London residence. Which building?

Buckingham Palace: Official London residence of the British monarch. Buckingham Palace (UK:) is the official residence and the administrative headquarters of the monarch of the United Kingdom in London.
Derived from the Latin word for 'to assess,' this systematic count of a population's members is recommended by the UN to be conducted at least once every ten years. What is it?
Census: Compilation of information about a given population.
Canada's tenth deputy prime minister, she negotiated the USMCA trade deal with the United States and Mexico while serving as foreign affairs minister — who is she?
Chrystia Freeland: Canadian politician and journalist (born 1968)

Fought in central and western Mexico from 1926 to 1929, this Catholic uprising erupted after President Calles moved to strictly enforce anticlerical articles of the 1917 constitution — what's this conflict called?

This organizational process shifts planning and decision-making authority away from a central group to smaller units, and applies across politics, business, and even monetary systems — what's it called?
This period of drier-than-normal weather can stretch from days to years, drying out wetlands, fueling larger wildfires, and battering both farms and local economies — what climate phenomenon is it?
Drought: Period with less precipitation than normal.
According to legend, this mythical city of gold got its name from a Muisca king who covered himself in gold dust before diving into a sacred Andean lake — what is it?
El Dorado: Legendary city in South America.
Named in the Synoptic Gospels as blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, this concept describes the one transgression Christian theologians agree can never be forgiven — what is it called?
Eternal sin: Sin which will never be forgiven by God.

Founded in 680–681 by a nomadic people led by Asparuh after they defeated a Byzantine army, which medieval Balkan state at its height stretched from the Danube Bend to the Black Sea and rivaled Byzantium for centuries?
First Bulgarian Empire: 681–1018 state in Southeast Europe.

Elected leader of the Social Democratic Party in 1913, this politician's support for war loans split his party before he became the first president of the newly declared German republic in 1919 — who was he?
Friedrich Ebert: President of Germany from 1919 to 1925.
This German chancellor from 1998 to 2005, who replaced the long-ruling Helmut Kohl, later drew fire for taking jobs with Russian state energy giants like Gazprom and Nord Stream — who is he?

Gerhard Schröder: Chancellor of Germany from 1998 to 2005. Gerhard Fritz Kurt "Gerd" Schröder (born 7 April 1944) is a German former politician and lobbyist who served as Chancellor of Germany from 1998 to 2005.
According to Arthurian legend, this queen of Great Britain was famously seduced by Mordred during his rebellion against her husband, King Arthur — who is she?
Guinevere: Arthurian legend character. Guinevere has continued to be a popular character featured in numerous adaptations of the legend since the 19th-century Arthurian revival.
Born in Lamar, Missouri, this vice president suddenly inherited the presidency in 1945 and went on to launch the Marshall Plan and NATO — who was he?
Harry S. Truman: President of the United States from 1945 to 1953.
Firstborn child of Cronus and Rhea, this virgin goddess of the hearth chose never to marry despite her status among the Twelve Olympians — who is she?
Hestia: Greek goddess of the hearth. In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Hestia (Ancient Greek: Ἑστία, lit. 'hearth, fireplace, altar') is the virgin goddess of the hearth and the home.
Co-founding a Marxist-Leninist political organization with Bobby Seale in 1966, this activist later earned a PhD in social philosophy citing Plato's Republic as an influence — who is he?
Huey P. Newton: Founder of the Black Panther Party (1942–1989)
In 1980, six gunmen demanding independence for a province of Iran stormed a London diplomatic compound, holding 26 hostages during a six-day standoff — which historic event?
Iranian Embassy siege: 1980 hostage situation in London.
The only surviving son of Emperor Akbar, this Mughal ruler was schooled in Chagatai, Persian and Hindustani before taking the throne and reigning from 1605 to 1627. Who is he?
Jahangir: Mughal emperor from 1605 to 1627. The third and only surviving son of Emperor Akbar I (r. 1556–1605) and his consort Maryam uz-Zamani.

A WWII Marine flying ace awarded the Navy Cross over Okinawa, this Mississippi politician later served as mayor of Biloxi and won a $500 million jury verdict against a rival funeral-home company — who is he?

Jeremiah Joseph O'Keefe: American politician. Jeremiah Joseph O'Keefe III (July 12, 1923 – August 23, 2016) was an American fighter ace, Democratic Party politician, insurance executive, and funeral director.

Elected vice president on the 1840 Whig ticket, this man became the tenth U.S. president just 31 days into his running mate's term after his sudden death — leaving him estranged from both major parties. Who was he?
John Tyler: President of the United States from 1841 to 1845.
After an 11-year career in the oil industry, this 105th Archbishop of Canterbury officiated the coronation of Charles III and the state funeral of Elizabeth II — who is he?
Justin Welby: Archbishop of Canterbury from 2013 to 2025.
As Abu Dhabi's ruler from 2004, this leader helped bring the Louvre, a New York University campus, and Etihad Airways to the emirate — who was he?
Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan: President of the United Arab Emirates from 2004 to 2022.

Medically retired from the Marines, this Medal of Honor recipient earned the nation's highest military honor for actions in Afghanistan's Helmand Province in 2010, making him the youngest living recipient — who is he?

Serving the state of Zhao during the Warring States period, this general — one of Chinese folklore's 'Four Greatest Generals' — died in 229 BC and is remembered as a master of defensive tactics. Who was he?
This Texan went from teacher to congressional aide to the U.S. House, then ascended from the vice presidency to the White House in 1963 after a president's assassination — who was he?
Lyndon B. Johnson: President of the United States from 1963 to 1969.
A billionaire Emirati royal and brother of the UAE's president, this sheikh holds stakes in football clubs around the world through the City Football Group — who is he?
Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan: Vice President of the United Arab Emirates.
Raised an Anglican though her parents had converted to Catholicism, this English queen ruled jointly with her husband — their reign remembered simply as "William and ___." Who was she?
Mary II: Queen of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1689 to 1694.
The longest-serving governor in Massachusetts history, this Democrat lost the 1988 presidential election to George H. W. Bush — who is he?
Michael Dukakis: American politician and lawyer (born 1933)
Once considered one of the finest ODI batsmen in the world, this Indian captain led three World Cup campaigns in the 1990s before a life ban for match-fixing ended his career — who is he?

Mohammad Azharuddin: Indian cricketer. Mohammad Azizuddin Azharuddin (born 8 February 1963) is an Indian politician and a former cricketer who also served as the Indian national cricket team's captain.
A former footballer and journalist before entering politics, this BJP leader served as the 12th Chief Minister of Manipur from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?
N. Biren Singh: Chief Minister of Manipur from 2017 to 2025. Joining politics in 2002, Biren joined the Democratic Revolutionary Peoples Party and won the assembly elections from Heingang.
A onetime metal worker who rose through Soviet ranks under Lazar Kaganovich, this leader shocked the world by denouncing Stalin and presided over the Cuban Missile Crisis — who was he?
Nikita Khrushchev: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964.

A boilermaker before West Point, this U.S. general graduated in 1915 alongside Dwight Eisenhower in "the class the stars fell on" and later became the first chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff — who is he?
Omar Bradley: United States Army general (1893–1981)

Born to a Tutsi family that fled to Uganda when he was two, this politician commanded a rebel force that ended the 1994 genocide in his home country and has served as its president since 2000 — who is he?
Paul Kagame: President of Rwanda since 2000. The RPF was one of the main belligerents of the Rwandan Civil War and was the armed force which ended the 1994 Rwandan genocide.
Educated in New Zealand and the United States, this Thai businessman led the Move Forward Party, successor to the dissolved Future Forward Party — who is he?
Pita Limjaroenrat: Thai businessman and politician (born 1980)

Known as Bilqis in Arabic and Makeda in Ge'ez, this Hebrew Bible figure brought a caravan of lavish gifts to King Solomon and is linked by modern historians to an ancient South Arabian kingdom in Yemen?
Queen of Sheba: Historical figure in the Abrahamic religions.
Widely considered the greatest mountaineer ever, who made the first solo ascent of Everest and was the first to climb all fourteen eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen?
Reinhold Messner: Italian mountaineer, adventurer and explorer (born 1944)

Born when Octavian rose to power and established the Augustan Principate in 27 BC, its western half fell in 476 AD while its eastern half lived on until Constantinople fell in 1453. What state is this?
Roman Empire: 27 BC–476/1453 AD state and civilization. The Roman Empire was a state that dominated the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa during the classical period.
Taken as a Mughal hostage at age nine to enforce his father's treaty, this man later ruled from 1681 to 1689 as the second king of a major Indian empire — who is he?
Sambhaji: Chhatrapati of the Marathas from 1681 to 1689.
Nicknamed both "the Blond" and "the Drunkard," this son of Suleiman the Magnificent saw Cyprus and Tunis conquered but suffered a famous naval loss at Lepanto — who was he?
Selim II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1566 to 1574.
Eldest daughter of King Amalric, this 12th-century ruler stood by her unpopular husband Guy of Lusignan even as her leprosy-stricken brother struggled to secure her succession — who is she?
Sibylla, Queen of Jerusalem: Crusader ruler from 1186 to 1190.

On 26 September 1983, this Soviet duty officer judged his early-warning system's report of incoming U.S. missiles to be a false alarm — disobeying protocol and likely averting nuclear war. Who was he?
Stanislav Petrov: Soviet Air Defence Forces officer (1939–2017)

Running from 1912 to 1926 and named for its reigning emperor, this period in Japanese history saw political power shift from a group of elder statesmen to the country's parliamentary parties — what do historians call it?
Taishō era: Period of Japanese history from 1912 to 1926.
Serving as Lord Chancellor before becoming Archbishop of Canterbury, this cleric clashed with King Henry II and was murdered by the king's men in 1170 — who was he?
Thomas Becket: Archbishop of Canterbury from 1162 to 1170.
After leading Turkey's main miners' union and briefly working at the World Bank, this engineer-turned-statesman served as prime minister before becoming president from 1989 to 1993 — who is he?
Turgut Özal: President of Turkey from 1989 to 1993. ANAP won a parliamentary majority in the 1983 general election and Özal subsequently became the prime minister of Turkey.
Serving as the 18th U.S. ambassador to NATO before rising to Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, this diplomat briefly served as acting deputy secretary of state in 2023 — who is she?
Sparked by a dispute over Maria Theresa's right to inherit the Habsburg throne, this 1740–1748 conflict began when Prussia seized the wealthy province of Silesia — what was this conflict called?
War of the Austrian Succession: 1740–1748 war between European powers.

Despite a huge edge in tanks and aircraft, the Soviet Union took heavy losses and was expelled from the League of Nations after its November 1939 invasion of Finland — what was this three-and-a-half-month conflict called?
Winter War: 1939–1940 war between the Soviet Union and Finland.
A career Army general who became a national hero in the Mexican-American War, this 12th U.S. president died of a stomach illness just 16 months into office — who is he?
Zachary Taylor: President of the United States from 1849 to 1850.

Joseph Schumpeter (born 1883) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Copernicium?
Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
What is the atomic number of Thallium?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
Which country is Panavia Tornado from?
Panavia Tornado: Italy. It first flew on 14 August 1974 and was introduced into service in 1979–1980.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.
Nicknamed the 'nail mosquito,' this genus — first classified in 1818 — is the sole mosquito genus known to carry human malaria — which genus is it?
Anopheles is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Ranging from 1 to 5 meters tall and found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, this shrub genus's best-known species is the European type also called barberry — what genus is it?
Berberis is a large genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs from 1-5 m (3+12-16+12 ft) tall, found throughout temperate and subtropical regions of the world (apart from Australia).
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.

Appearing in early childhood with symptoms like poor coordination and stiff or weak muscles, this group of movement disorders does not worsen over time even though symptoms become more noticeable in a child's first years — which condition?
Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Sometimes triggered by lead poisoning or reactions to neuroleptic drugs, this neurological disorder produces involuntary, twisting muscle contractions — what is it?

Dystonia is a neurological hyperkinetic movement disorder in which sustained or repetitive muscle contractions occur involuntarily, resulting in twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal fixed postures.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?
The excessive buildup of collagen-rich connective tissue after chronic inflammation or repeated injury, leaving a permanent scar that can choke off organ function — what's this process called?
Fibrosis is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.
Sometimes mistakenly called the 'stomach flu' even though it's unrelated to influenza, this inflammation of the gut is usually viral, with rotavirus the top cause in children. What condition is it?
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and intestine.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.
About the size of an almond in humans, this small brain region links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus (pl.: hypothalami; from Ancient Greek (hup) 'under' and (thlamos) 'chamber') is a small part of the vertebrate brain that contains a number of nuclei with a variety of functions.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.

Seen using a silver stain and grown on media containing the amino acid cysteine, this genus of bacteria causes a severe pneumonia-like illness as well as a milder flu-like illness called Pontiac fever — name the genus?
Legionella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria that can be seen using a silver stain or grown in a special media that contains cysteine, an amino acid.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
An autosomal dominant flaw in the fibrillin-making FBN1 gene gives this disorder its tell-tale look — tall, long-limbed, double-jointed — while quietly threatening the aorta — what is it?
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multi-systemic genetic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this condition wears down joint cartilage over years, often first striking the knuckles nearest your fingertips and the base of the thumb — what is it?
Osteoarthritis is a type of degenerative joint disease that results from breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.

Caused by the loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15, this rare genetic disorder leads to weak muscles and poor feeding in infancy, then constant hunger and risk of obesity in childhood — what's it called?

Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15. A similar mechanism occurs in Angelman syndrome, except the defective chromosome 15 is from the mother, or two copies are from the father.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.
Caused by a lack of vitamin C, this deficiency disease shows up after about a month of poor diet with weakness, sore limbs, gum disease, and bleeding from the skin — what is it?
Scurvy is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
This Taiwanese-American software engineer co-founded and served as CTO of a massively popular video-sharing platform before later building MixBit through his company AVOS Systems — who is he?
Steve Chen (Wade-; born August 25, 1978) is a Taiwanese-American software engineer and Internet entrepreneur who is a co-founder and ex-CTO of YouTube.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Formed when acetic acid combines with a base, this ion is also nature's most common building block for biosynthesis — what is it?
Acetate: Salt formed from acetic acid and a base.
Also known as thymol seeds, bishop's weed, or carom, this Apiaceae herb's fruit is often mistaken for lovage seed — what is it?
Sometimes called 'pigweed,' this genus of plants is grown worldwide as a leaf vegetable and for its edible grain — which genus?
Amaranth: Genus of plants. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a succulent, hollow stem.
Named by paleontologist Barnum Brown in 1908, this armored dinosaur is considered the archetypal member of its group despite no complete skeleton ever being found — which genus?
Ankylosaurus: Ankylosaurid dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Period.
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.
This genus of early African hominins, which lived during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, is considered ancestral to the genus that includes modern humans — which genus?
Australopithecus: Genus of hominin ancestral to modern humans. The genera Homo (which includes modern humans), Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus evolved from some Australopithecus species.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary facial paralysis droops one side of the face and can heighten sensitivity to sound — what condition is it?
Bell's palsy: Facial paralysis. Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
This organ stores urine received from the kidneys via the ureters before it exits through the urethra, and gives us the medical term 'cystitis' when inflamed — what is it?
Bladder: Organ in vertebrates that collects and stores urine from the kidneys before disposal.
Typically housed in the head near the organs for vision, hearing, and smell, this organ processes thought and cognition while coordinating muscle activity — which organ?
Brain: Organ central to the nervous system.
Discovered in 1817 simultaneously by two German chemists as an impurity in zinc carbonate, this soft silvery-white metal shares chemical traits with zinc and mercury — which element?
Cadmium: Chemical element with atomic number 48 (Cd)
Called the 'father of modern taxonomy,' which Swedish biologist formalized the two-name system for naming living things and was later ennobled as von Linné?
Carl Linnaeus: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778)
First flown in 1955 as a tricycle-gear evolution of an earlier taildragger model, this four-seat high-wing aircraft is the most-produced plane in history — which model is it?
Cessna 172: Propeller driven single engine aircraft.

Most often documented in boxers and football players, this neurodegenerative disease is linked to repeated blows to the head and can worsen into dementia — what's its name, usually shortened to three letters?
Chronic traumatic encephalopathy: Neurodegenerative disease caused by head injury.
Native to tropical Africa and Asia, this plant genus produces caffeine-rich seeds that are roasted and brewed into one of the world's most valuable traded commodities — which genus?

Describing how closely two variables move together, this statistical measure is famously not proof of causation, and two variables can even be linked this way without truly depending on each other — what is it called?
Correlation: Statistical relationship. In statistics, correlation is a type of statistical relationship between two random variables or bivariate data.
Making up about 80 percent water and mostly colorless, this catch-all term covers everything inside a cell's outer membrane except its nucleus — what is it?
Cytoplasm: All of the contents of a cell including organelles but excluding the nucleus.
Carnations and sweet williams both belong to which flowering plant genus of about 340 species, native mainly to Europe and Asia?
This Eastern Han hydrologist is credited as the first to harness a waterwheel to power the bellows of a blast furnace for forging cast iron — who was this ingenious engineer?
Du Shi: 1st-century engineer, metallurgist and politician.
The second-largest member of the deer family, this animal is also called "wapiti," a Shawnee and Cree word meaning "white rump" for the pale fur it flashes to signal alarm — what animal is it?
Elk: Species of deer. The word "elk" originally referred to the European variety of the moose, Alces alces, but was transferred to Cervus canadensis by North American colonists.

In 2019 this French-American MIT economist shared the Nobel with her husband and Michael Kremer for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty, rooted in the randomized trials of her J-PAL lab — who is she?
This front-of-the-head body part houses most sense organs — eyes, nose, and mouth — and its damage or scarring can profoundly affect a person's sense of identity. What is it?
Face: Front of a head. The face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
This normal, occasionally embarrassing bodily process brings intestinal gas to the rectum, pressurizes it with muscle contractions, and releases it through the anus — what is it?
Flatulence: Bodily function of expelling intestinal gas from the anus.

After dropping out of Harvard to help build early versions of Windows at Microsoft, this developer co-founded a studio that made Half-Life and later launched a digital storefront called Steam — who is he?
Known only from teeth and four jawbones, this extinct genus of giant ape roamed China for nearly two million years and is now thought to be a close relative of the orangutan — what is it?
Gigantopithecus: Extinct genus of primate. The species may have been sexually dimorphic, with males much bigger than females.

Native from Mexico down to southern Brazil, this large arboreal lizard can grow past six feet long, is a popular but demanding pet, and has become invasive in many warm regions worldwide — which species?
Green iguana: Species of reptile. Usually, this animal is simply called the iguana.

Named after a bird of prey, this British-developed attack aircraft was the only truly successful vertical-takeoff design of its era, able to fly from car parks and forest clearings instead of vulnerable airbases — which aircraft?
Harrier jump jet: Multirole combat aircraft family by Hawker Siddeley, later British Aerospace.
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
This huge insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, and its females often carry an egg-laying tube that doubles as a stinger — what order is it?
Hymenoptera: Order of insects. Over 150,000 living species of Hymenoptera have been described, in addition to over 2,000 extinct ones.
An application of computer science, this field covers not just computers and networks but also distribution technologies like television and telephones — what is it?
Information technology: Computer-based technologies. Whisler commented that "the new technology does not yet have a single established name.
Sometimes called the founder of pneumatic chemistry, this 17th-century Brussels physician coined the word 'gas' and ran a famous five-year willow-tree experiment. Who was he?
Jan Baptist van Helmont: Chemist and physician (1580–1644)
Equal to the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre, this SI unit of energy is named for a 19th-century English physicist — which unit?
Joule: SI unit of energy. The joule ( JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
This colorless noble gas defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983, based on the wavelength of one of its spectral lines — which element?
Krypton: Chemical element with atomic number 36 (Kr)

Originally cultivated by the ancient Egyptians and now grown worldwide with China producing over half the crop, this leafy Asteraceae vegetable also has a stem-focused variety called celtuce — name the vegetable?
Lettuce: Species of annual plant of the daisy family, most often grown as a leaf vegetable.
Also called dragon's eye, this tropical fruit tree from the soapberry family produces fruit similar to lychee but with a milder aroma, and is native to Southeast Asia and southern China — what is it?
Longan: Species of tropical fruit-bearing tree.
Transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes and caused by single-celled Plasmodium parasites, which disease's symptoms typically begin 10 to 15 days after infection?

Selected in 1969 as a dedicated air-superiority fighter and first flown in 1972, this twin-engine American jet boasts a staggering combat record of 106 victories and zero losses — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle: Multirole and air superiority fighter family.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)

It strikes when blood flow to the heart muscle stops, killing tissue — classically a crushing chest pain that radiates to the left arm or jaw, though women more often feel only neck pain or fatigue. What is this medical emergency?
Myocardial infarction: Interruption of cardiac blood supply.
A vitamer of vitamin B3 that the body can build from tryptophan, in large prescription doses it lowers LDL and raises "good" HDL cholesterol — what's this compound also called niacin?
Nicotinic acid: Organic compound and a form of vitamin B3.
Native to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this striped mammal looks like a zebra crossbred with a giraffe but is actually the giraffe's closest living relative — which animal?
Okapi: Species of mammal. Although the okapi has striped markings reminiscent of zebras, it is most closely related to the giraffe.

Produced in the hypothalamus and nicknamed for its role in love and social bonding, this peptide hormone also doubles as a pharmaceutical that speeds up childbirth by triggering uterine contractions — what is it?
Oxytocin: Peptide hormone and neuropeptide. Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Its name comes from the Greek for 'making,' and it leans on devices like assonance, alliteration, and metre to evoke meanings beyond the literal — what literary art is this?
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.
Discovered in 1861 via flame spectroscopy by Bunsen and Kirchhoff, this alkali metal is named from the Latin word for 'deep red' — which element?
Rubidium: Chemical element with atomic number 37 (Rb)
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.

Recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909, this small, clever herding dog breed originated in Scotland's northern isles and was originally called by a different collie name before breeders objected — which breed?
Shetland Sheepdog: Scottish breed of dog. The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?
Shaped roughly like a necktie and made up of the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process, which flat bone protects the heart and lungs at the front of the rib cage?
Sternum: Flat bone in the middle front part of the rib cage.
Closely related to privet and native from southeastern Europe to eastern Asia, which flowering shrub genus, commonly called lilacs, hosts caterpillars like the privet hawk moth?
Syringa: Genus of flowering plants in the lilac family.
This vertebrate group includes every amphibian and amniote — even limbless descendants like snakes, which still count as members through their four-limbed ancestry — what's the clade called?
Tetrapod: Clade of the first four-limbed vertebrates and their descendants.
Known for dry, bumpy skin studded with parotoid glands and a more terrestrial lifestyle than its smooth-skinned cousins, what is this amphibian called?
Toad: Common name for certain frogs, especially of the family Bufonidae.
Known to NATO as the 'Badger,' this twin-engined Soviet jet bomber has flown for nearly 70 years and lives on today as China's license-built H-6 — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-16: Soviet heavy bomber. The Tupolev Tu-16 (USAF/DOD reporting name Type 39; NATO reporting name: Badger) is a twin-engined jet strategic heavy bomber used by the Soviet Union.

First published in 1797 by an Italian physicist, this phenomenon describes how a fluid's pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrowing pipe — an example of Bernoulli's principle at work in everything from atomizers to wine aerators. What's it called?
Venturi effect: Reduced pressure caused by a flow restriction in a tube or pipe.
Packing a mass comparable to the Sun into a volume the size of Earth, this dense stellar remnant glows from leftover heat rather than nuclear fusion — what is it?
White dwarf: Stellar core remnant. A white dwarf is a very dense type of star: in an Earth-sized volume, it packs a mass that is comparable to the Sun.
Known by the formula ZnO, this white, water-insoluble powder shows up in sunscreens, calamine lotion, and rubber manufacturing — which compound?
Zinc oxide: White powder insoluble in water. Although it occurs naturally as the mineral zincite, most zinc oxide is produced synthetically.
The symbol for ruthenium is Ru. Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
The symbol for zinc is Zn. Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.

Alain Delon: Alain Fabien Maurice Marcel Delon (French: [alɛ̃ dəlɔ̃]; 8 November 1935 – 18 August 2024) was a French actor, film producer, screenwriter, singer, and businessman.
In what year did Ray Stevenson die?
Ray Stevenson: George Raymond Stevenson (25 May 1964 – 21 May 2023) was a British actor, best known for his film and television work.
